0.title: Interactive Sync Review & Deletion Diff Visualizer
0.content: Standard automated sync daemons run unattended in background crons. When an unexpected deletion wave occurs—such as an operator accidentally moving a root directory or an external service wiping a folder—unattended sync immediately replicates the wipe across all replicas. Bisync Hub introduces an interactive human-in-the-loop inspection barrier before destructive mutations are committed.

1.title: How It Works
1.content: [ Trigger Sync ] ──► [ Dry-Run Operation ] ──► [ Parse Mutation List ] │ ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ Deletions <= Max Threshold Deletions > Max Threshold │ │ ▼ ▼ [ Auto-Apply Policies ] [ HALT & Emit Review Event ] │ ▼ [ Operator Decision Modal ] • Confirm Specific Deletes • Reject / Abort Run • Override Heuristics .

2.title: 1. Dry-Run Mutation Analysis
2.content: Every scheduled or manual sync cycle executes in --dry-run inspection mode first. The engine streams the stdout/stderr mutation log and categorizes every proposed operation: . | + CREATE: New file appearing on either Path1 or Path2. | ~ MODIFY: Content or metadata discrepancy requiring replication. | - DELETE: Proposed removal of a file or directory. | .

3.title: 2. High-Severity Quota Halts
3.content: If proposed deletions exceed either: . | The absolute file limit (e.g. SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_COUNT=25), or | The directory percentage ratio (e.g. SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_RATIO=0.10), | . the sync engine immediately trips the circuit breaker, writes an atomic .review_pending state, and emits real-time WebSocket notifications to the management dashboard. See Customizable Safety Policies for policy details.

4.title: 3. Granular Operator Triage
4.content: Operators can open the Web Dashboard review modal to: . | Inspect file diffs, file sizes, and last modified timestamps side-by-side. | View intelligent heuristic evaluations (e.g. temporary lock file detection, canary protection, user local deletion identification). | Selectively confirm specific deletions, restore/reject items, or auto-apply heuristic recommendations in batch. | Stage atomic pre-mutation backups and trigger an authorized force sync directly from the modal. | . Safety Guarantee: No file is ever removed when a review threshold is tripped until an authorized operator explicitly signs off or an automated timeout policy executes an abort.

11.title: Multi-Analyzer Heuristic Conflict Engine
11.content: Most bidirectional sync tools rely on a naive, binary rule: “newer timestamp wins”. In distributed cloud environments, this rule causes silent data loss because: . | Cloud storage APIs (e.g. Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, SharePoint) round timestamps to 1-second or 2-second windows or update them asynchronously. | Device clocks can drift or suffer skew during daylight savings transitions. | Rapid concurrent edits on mobile and desktop produce collisions where the “newer” file is actually an incomplete draft. | . Bisync Hub replaces timestamp gambling with a multi-analyzer heuristic confidence engine.

12.title: The Evaluation Pipeline
12.content: When both Path1 and Path2 report modifications to the same file path, the engine executes four independent heuristic analyzers: . | Heuristic Analyzer | Signal Analyzed | Weight | Description | . | SizeDivergenceAnalyzer | Content volume delta | 30% | Detects dramatic file shrinks or expansions indicating truncation or major additions. | . | BinarySignatureAnalyzer | MIME & header magic bytes | 25% | Verifies format validity (e.g. SQLite database header, JPEG signatures) to penalize corrupt partial writes. | . | ClockSkewAnalyzer | Cross-remote timestamp drift | 25% | Evaluates cloud API timestamp granularity and compensates for known provider skews (e.g., OneDrive 2s window). | . | VelocityAnalyzer | Modification frequency | 20% | Scores edit frequency to distinguish steady active editing from stale background touches. | .

13.title: Confidence Calculation & Safety Bands
13.content: The engine aggregates individual analyzer scores into a unified Confidence Index (0% - 100%): . Score >= 85% ──► [ HIGH CONFIDENCE ] ──► Auto-resolve in favor of dominant replica 60% - 84% ──► [ MEDIUM CONFIDENCE ] ──► Auto-resolve; backup displaced candidate to .bisync_backup/ Score < 60% ──► [ LOW CONFIDENCE ] ──► QUARANTINE: Preserve in .bisync_quarantine/ & prompt Operator .

14.title: Safety Features
14.content: . | Deterministic Quarantine: Unresolvable collisions (Score < 60%) are safely moved into a .bisync_quarantine/ isolation jail for operator review. | Conflict Backup Preserves: For medium-confidence resolutions (60%–84%), the displaced version is backed up to .bisync_backup/ before overwriting. | Clock Skew Tolerance: Built-in compensation algorithms for cloud timestamp drift and DST shifts. | . All heuristic scoring weights and confidence thresholds are fully configurable in bisync.env to match your organization’s risk tolerance.

16.title: Customizable Safety Policies & Circuit Breakers
16.content: ● Shipped & Active . Core Safety Tenets: Pre-execution canary protection (RCLONE_TEST), path confinement filesystem jails, and pre-mutation deletion quotas (SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_COUNT, SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_RATIO) are fully active in the core engine. Dynamic in-dashboard parameter configuration is tracked on the Roadmap. Automated tools must know when to stop. Running bidirectional synchronization when a network share is unmounted, when a cloud provider returns HTTP 429 rate limits, or when a disk is failing will corrupt sync state and trigger cascading deletions. Bisync Hub implements a two-stage defensive policy barrier: Pre-Execution and Pre-Mutation.

18.title: 1. Pre-Execution Validation Gates
18.content: Before invoking any sync or check command, Bisync Hub checks environmental invariants: . | Canary File Verification (RCLONE_TEST): . | Requires a known marker file to exist on both local and remote mount roots. | If a network volume unmounts or cloud sync token expires, the canary file disappears. The engine detects this and aborts instantly, preventing the empty directory from being treated as a mass deletion. | . | Path Confinement (Filesystem Jail): . | All local file manipulations are strictly validated with filepath.Rel and prefix checks to ensure zero path traversal escapes outside designated sync roots. | . | Advisory POSIX Locking (flock): . | Prevents overlapping sync jobs from corrupting local metadata or triggering race conditions across systemd timers or manual CLI runs. | . | .

19.title: 2. Pre-Mutation Circuit Breakers
19.content: During sync execution, incoming mutation requests pass through configurable circuit breakers: . # bisync.env safety settings SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_COUNT=25 # Hard limit on total file removals per run SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_RATIO=0.10 # Maximum 10% of total files may be deleted SAFETY_ENABLE_CANARY=true # Canary file mandatory on both remotes SAFETY_RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF=true # Exponential backoff on provider HTTP 429 .

20.title: 3. Automatic Backoff & Quarantine
20.content: . | Provider Throttling: When Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive signals rate limits (429 Too Many Requests), Bisync Hub immediately halts further calls and enforces exponential backoff with jitter. | Fail-Safe Abort: Any violation of a safety policy halts execution cleanly and logs the event to the audit ledger. | . Zero Canary Bypass Policy: Canary check routines are hardcoded to fail-closed. If canary status is ambiguous, sync execution is blocked.

22.title: Cryptographic Immutable Audit Ledger
22.content: ● Shipped & Available . Production Ledger: The Cryptographic Immutable Audit Ledger is fully implemented and included in the native binary. Every synchronization action, conflict resolution, and file mutation is cryptographically sealed into an append-only SQLite database backed by SHA-256 hash chains. Compliance, security audits, and forensic debugging require an undeniable, tamper-evident record of all storage mutations: Who deleted file X? When was conflict Y resolved? What was the decision confidence score? . Bisync Hub embeds an immutable, SQLite-backed cryptographic ledger with trigger-enforced append-only constraints.

24.title: 1. SQLite Trigger-Enforced Immutability
24.content: The internal SQLite database employs schema-level BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers on audit tables: . CREATE TRIGGER prevent_ledger_tampering BEFORE UPDATE ON audit_events BEGIN SELECT RAISE(FAIL, 'FATAL: audit_events table is strictly append-only.'); END; . Even if an attacker or misconfigured script gains write access to the database file, existing audit entries cannot be modified or purged without breaking database integrity.

25.title: 2. SHA-256 Hash Chaining
25.content: Each audit entry computes a SHA-256 digest over the concatenation of: . | Previous_Record_Hash | Event_Type and Timestamp (UTC millisecond precision) | Payload_JSON (redacted secrets, sanitized paths, decision scores) | . The application provides a built-in cryptographic verification command (bisync-hub verify-ledger) to audit chain integrity and identify any external byte tampering.

26.title: 3. Redaction by Default
26.content: All sensitive credentials—including RC_PASS, OAuth refresh tokens, webhook URLs, and private auth headers—are recursively redacted via security.RedactSecrets before entering the audit stream. The audit ledger ensures full compliance with operational standards while protecting organizational data sovereignty.

35.title: Core Capabilities
35.content: . | Dual Transport (stdio & Embedded SSE): Local agents (Cline, Claude Desktop, Cursor) can spawn bisync-hub mcp over stdio, while remote or multi-agent setups can connect to the embedded SSE endpoint served alongside the dashboard daemon. | Parameter-Fingerprinted Confirmation Tickets: Destructive or state-altering calls (bisync_trigger_sync with resync/force, bisync_resolve_review with execute=true, or mutating bisync_dedupe_by_hash modes) require a two-step confirmation flow. 40.title: Architecture & Safety Principles
40.content: Bisync Hub is built on the assumption that networks drop, cloud APIs return unexpected responses, and distributed clocks drift. Every subsystem follows three core tenets: . | Visibility Before Action: Never mutate storage silently without pre-flight inspection and an immutable audit trail. | Safety Before Automation: Halt immediately when an invariant is violated (such as a missing canary file or high deletion threshold) rather than guessing. | Defense in Depth: Isolate local paths, serialize concurrent executions, and scrub secrets at every boundary. | .

42.title: Filesystem Path Confinement Jails
42.content: Local file browsing and sync operations enforce strict root containment so relative traversal (../) or escape paths cannot step outside configured directories: . relPath, err := filepath.Rel(jailRoot, targetPath) if err != nil || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, "..") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, "/") { return ErrPathTraversalViolation } . Any boundary violation is rejected immediately and recorded in the audit ledger.

43.title: POSIX Advisory Process Locking
43.content: To prevent race conditions between scheduled background runs, manual CLI commands, and concurrent profile actions, Bisync Hub uses non-blocking POSIX advisory locks (flock with LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) per lock target, with stale-lock cleanup after abnormal exits and fail-fast reporting on active contention.

44.title: Secret Redaction
44.content: Inputs, configuration payloads, error messages, and logs pass through recursive sanitization (security.RedactSecrets), masking sensitive fields (PASS, TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, CREDENTIAL) as [REDACTED] before persistence or external emission.

45.title: MCP Confirmation Ticket Gating
45.content: AI agents connecting over Model Context Protocol (stdio or embedded SSE) cannot trigger destructive operations (trigger_sync with resync/force, resolve_review, dedupe_by_hash) without passing a two-step confirmation flow: . | Parameter Fingerprinting: Tickets bind to SHA256(canonical(params))—any change to flags or arguments invalidates the ticket. | Short TTL & Read-Only Mode: Tickets expire automatically after 5 minutes, and launching with MCP_READ_ONLY=true disables mutating tool registration completely. | .

47.title: Finite State Machine (FSM) & Queue Orchestrator
47.content: Workload execution is governed by an explicit state machine rather than ad-hoc shell scripts: . idle → validating → running → review_required / completed / failed / aborted . | Invalid Transition Guarding: Disallowed state transitions are rejected at the engine level. | Concurrency & Cancellation: A bounded queue orchestrator prevents per-profile lock collisions while context cancellation cleanly stops active subprocesses and restores canary state on abort. | .

48.content: Duplicate detection supports both content hashes (MD5 / SHA-256) and size-plus-filename matching for remotes without native checksum support. Results group into collapsible clusters with staged actions (keep-local, keep-remote, keep-both, newest, oldest) backed by confirmation checks before deletion.

54.title: Why Not Just Run a Cron Script?
54.content: Cron scripts are ubiquitous, but they fail silently when edge cases occur: . | The Unmounted Mount Disaster: If an NFS/SMB share or rclone mount disconnects, an automated cron script sees an empty folder and issues deletions for thousands of files across the remote replica. | The Cloud Timestamp Shift: Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive report timestamps differently than local ext4/APFS filesystems. A simple script relying on test fileA -nt fileB frequently overwrites valid changes. | Overlapping Job Corruption: If a sync run takes longer than the cron interval (e.g., due to large video uploads), concurrent sync instances access the cache simultaneously, corrupting .bisync lock state. | . Bisync Hub eliminates every one of these failure modes out of the box.

90.title: Option A: Automated Installer (Linux)
90.content: Downloads the latest signed binary, verifies checksums, and configures systemd integration: . # Standard installation (uses existing Rclone on PATH) curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slemmercs/rclone-bisync/main/deploy/install.sh | sudo bash # Or install Rclone automatically if not present curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slemmercs/rclone-bisync/main/deploy/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --install-rclone . View Installer CLI Options | Option | Description | Default | . | -i, --install-rclone | Install official Rclone binary if not found in PATH | false | . | -n, --dry-run | Simulate installation without modifying system | false | . | -d, --target-dir [path] | Installation target directory | $HOME/bisync-hub | . | --port [port] | Dashboard HTTP service port | 8080 | . | --skip-services | Stage binary and config without enabling systemd units | false | . | --min-rclone-version [ver] | Minimum required Rclone semver |   | . | --max-rclone-version [ver] | Maximum compatible Rclone semver |   | . | -y, --non-interactive | Run unattended with defaults | false | .

91.title: Option B: Manual Binary Download (Linux & macOS)
91.content: Download the standalone binary directly from GitHub Releases: . # Linux (x86_64) — use 'darwin-arm64' or 'darwin-amd64' for macOS curl -LO https://github.com/slemmercs/rclone-bisync/releases/latest/download/bisync-hub-linux-amd64 chmod +x bisync-hub-linux-amd64 sudo mv bisync-hub-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/bisync-hub .

92.title: 2. Configuration (bisync.env)
92.content: Create a working directory and generate your bisync.env configuration file: . mkdir -p ~/bisync && cd ~/bisync . # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ # Bisync Hub Core Configuration # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ PORT=8080 BIND_ADDR=127.0.0.1 # Default Sync Paths (Additional profiles can be added in the Web UI) PATH1=/home/operator/data PATH2=onedrive:data_backup # Safety & Circuit Breakers SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_COUNT=25 SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_RATIO=0.10 SAFETY_ENABLE_CANARY=true CANARY_FILENAME=RCLONE_TEST # Conflict Engine Settings CONFLICT_AUTO_RESOLVE_MIN_CONFIDENCE=0.85 CONFLICT_BACKUP_LOSERS=true # Embedded MCP Server MCP_READ_ONLY=false # Notification Webhooks # WEBHOOK_URL=https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...

93.title: 3. Starting the Server
93.content: Launch the management cockpit interactively or run a one-off dry-run simulation: . # Start the operational dashboard & scheduler bisync-hub dashboard --env-file bisync.env # Or test synchronization safely in dry-run mode bisync-hub sync --dry-run --env-file bisync.env . Open http://localhost:8080 in your browser to access the dashboard, verify remote OAuth status, and trigger your initial baseline sync. First-Time Sync Note: If syncing two non-empty directories for the first time, trigger an initial Resync from the profile card in the dashboard (or pass --resync on the CLI) to establish the baseline state cache. Storage Remotes Remote health checks & OAuth indicators Dual-Pane Explorer Browse local and remote directories .

94.title: 4. Running as a Background Service (Systemd)
94.content: If you used manual binary installation on Linux, create a systemd unit for 24/7 background operation (replace operator with your Linux username): . # /etc/systemd/system/bisync-hub.service [Unit] Description=Bisync Hub Cloud Orchestrator After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target [Service] Type=simple User=operator WorkingDirectory=/home/operator/bisync ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/bisync-hub dashboard --env-file /home/operator/bisync/bisync.env Restart=always RestartSec=10 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target . Enable and start the service: . sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now bisync-hub .

95.title: 5. Connecting AI Agents (MCP)
95.content: Bisync Hub includes a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server supporting both local stdio and embedded HTTP SSE transports.

96.title: Local Agents (stdio — Cline, Claude Desktop, Cursor)
96.content: Add Bisync Hub to your MCP client configuration (e.g., ~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json): . { "mcpServers": { "bisync-hub": { "command": "/usr/local/bin/bisync-hub", "args": ["mcp", "--env-file", "/home/operator/bisync/bisync.env"], "disabled": false } } } .

97.title: Network / Remote Agents (Embedded SSE)
97.content: When bisync-hub dashboard is running, the embedded MCP SSE endpoint is automatically served on port 8081 alongside the daemon—no separate background process required. Open the MCP Inspector pill in the dashboard header for one-click client snippets and live tool inspection.
